reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 28 question-paper pages and PDF pages 21–44 of the combined Ordinary Level scheme (the Paper 2 title page 21, the Paper 2 scale table on page 22, the summary of mark allocations on page 23, every Paper 2 model solution and marking note on pages 24–41, the Irish-language bonus table on page 42 and the blank back pages). Each task boundary is the published scale beside its model solution, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: The 2020 Leaving Certificate examinations were cancelled and replaced by Calculated Grades, but the SEC published this paper and its marking scheme. The paper is 300 marks: candidates answer all nine questions (Section A Q1–6, 25 marks each; Section B Q7 55 marks, Q8 55 marks, Q9 40 marks). Every question is retained.
40 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 23.

Bands from the Paper 2 scale table on scheme page 22 and the ladders printed beside each part: 5A 0,5; 5B 0,2,5; 5C 0,3,4,5; 5D 0,2,3,4,5; 10B 0,5,10; 10C 0,4,8,10; 10D 0,3,5,8,10; 20D 0,5,10,15,20. The page 22 table misprints the 10D ladder as “0, 3, 15, 8, 10”; every 10D part prints “Scale 10D (0, 3, 5, 8, 10)” beside its solution, which the cards follow.

This paper had no authored cards before this review; all 40 units are new. Marking points are lifted line by line from the scheme (read through the glyph repair map) and labelled with the part of the scheme they come from. Where the scheme stacks a fraction across lines that the provenance reader cannot rejoin, a bullet is quoted in two consecutive pieces (Q8(a)(i) high partial credit). Data tables are carried in the stem as the printed values. Q8(b)(v) is a pie-chart drawing; its card carries the printed credit criteria.
The question booklet is LC003GLP200EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003GLP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 1. All page references are PDF positions, which match the printed scheme page numbers.

cards.stem: A restaurant is offering a three-course meal consisting of one starter, one main course and one dessert. There are 4 different starters, 6 different main courses and 8 different desserts to choose from.
cards.questionText: How many different three-course meal combinations are available?

cards.questionText: When Jack visits the restaurant he discovers that the restaurant still has the 4 starters and the 6 main courses available but is sold out of some of the desserts. Jack now has 120 different three-course meal combinations to choose from. How many different desserts are still available to Jack?
